meta.title: Human–AI collaboration
meta.tagline: Humans alone vs. AI alone vs. humans + AI on decision tasks — the Vaccaro, Almaatouq & Malone (2024) extraction protocol, extended for generative AI.
meta.description: One experiment per entry, one human–AI condition per sub-entry, one performance measure per table row. Extracts the study design, the task, the participants, the AI system and how it was presented, and the mean / SD / N of human-alone, AI-alone and human–AI performance, so that synergy (human–AI vs. the better of the two) can be computed downstream. Field names follow the original codebook (Exp_Design, Comp_Type, Avg_Perf_HumanAI, …) so exports merge with the existing dataset. Two variables go beyond it: LLM_Model and Interaction_Mode; N_AI is added for AI systems evaluated over several runs.

entries.label: Experiment
entries.help: a study with its own participant sample and task; papers often report several (Study 1, Experiment 2, a replication). A re-analysis of the same data is not a new experiment.
entries.title: Experiment {Exp_ID} · {Task_Desc}

fields.name: Exp_ID
fields.label: Experiment id
fields.help: the paper's own label ('1', '2', 'Study 1', 'Experiment 2b'); use '1' when the paper reports a single experiment

fields.name: Exp_Design
fields.label: Design
fields.help: how the human-alone vs. human–AI comparison was assigned. Between-Subjects = different participants in each arm; Within-Subjects = the same participants did both; Mixed, … = the study has both kinds of factor — pick the variant that applies to the human vs. human–AI contrast; Other = team-level units, simulated pairings, or anything else

fields.name: Comp_Type
fields.label: Comparison
fields.help: Independent Samples when the human-alone and human–AI values come from different people; Dependent Samples when from the same people — within-subjects designs, and designs where the same individuals' own answers are later fused with the AI's

fields.name: N_Exp
fields.label: N (experiment)
fields.help: total number of human participants analysed in the experiment, all arms together

fields.name: Task_Desc
fields.label: Task
fields.help: one verb-first phrase: 'Detect deceptive hotel reviews', 'Diagnose a patient case from a vignette', 'Decide whether two face photos show the same person'

fields.name: Task_Data
fields.label: Task input
fields.help: modality of the material the human judges — all that apply

fields.name: Task_Output
fields.label: Task output
fields.help: form of the required answer: Binary (two classes), Categoric (more than two), Numeric (an estimate, rating or score), Text / Image / Code (open-ended production, even when it is later scored by a rubric)

fields.name: Task_Type
fields.label: Task type
fields.help: Decide = the answer is scored against a reference answer or an expert rubric (classification, detection, prediction, estimation, diagnosis, structured clinical or legal reasoning); Create = open-ended production judged on quality (writing, summarising, code, designs). This review includes Decide tasks only — record Create anyway so the exclusion is visible

fields.name: AI_Data_In
fields.label: AI input
fields.help: what the AI receives; it may differ from what the human sees (the AI reads the image, the human a report)

fields.name: AI_Data_Out
fields.label: AI output
fields.help: what the AI produces for the human: a class (Binary / Categorical), a number, probability or score (Numeric), free text such as a chat answer or rationale (Text), an image or heat-map (Image), code

fields.name: Participant_Type
fields.label: Participants
fields.help: the paper's own description: 'Crowdworkers', 'Practising attending physicians and residents', 'Radiologists (attending)'

fields.name: Participant_Type_2
fields.label: Participant group
fields.help: Specialists (Expert) = professionals with domain expertise in the task (physicians on a medical task, lawyers on a legal task); Specialists (Non-Expert) = professionals in training or working outside their specialty; Working Professionals = employees doing a work task that needs no domain expertise; Volunteers = unpaid members of the public

fields.name: Participant_Source
fields.label: Recruitment
fields.help: recruitment channel as stated: MTurk, Prolific, Upwork, Invitation, Email Lists, University, Hospital, Company, Volunteer, Not Specified

fields.name: Participant_Expert
fields.label: Domain experts
fields.help: true if the participants had domain expertise for the task

fields.name: Exp_Notes
fields.label: Experiment notes
fields.help: anything a coder must know: exclusions, which arms became conditions, reference arms that are missing or shared across conditions, unusual designs, discrepancies between text and tables

children.label: Human–AI condition
children.help: one arm in which humans worked WITH the AI. Human-alone arms and AI-alone runs are reference arms, not conditions — their values go into each condition's measure rows
children.title: {Condition_Name}

fields.name: Condition_Name
fields.label: Condition
fields.help: the paper's label for the arm: 'Physicians + GPT-4', 'HAI = Signed + predicted label', 'Fusion with ChatGPT'; with a single human–AI arm, name it after the AI

fields.name: AI_Type
fields.label: AI type
fields.help: Generative = a large language model or other generative model (GPT-4, GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT with vision, diffusion models); Deep = a non-generative neural network (CNN, BERT classifier); Shallow = classical machine learning (logistic regression, SVM, random forest); Wizard of Oz = simulated AI whose outputs were scripted or fixed by the experimenters

fields.name: LLM_Model
fields.label: AI model
fields.help: (beyond the original codebook) the specific system with version and access route: 'GPT-4 via ChatGPT Plus', 'GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06) via API in a custom app', 'Claude-3-Opus', 'ChatGPT (GPT-4V) chat interface'; null if not stated

fields.name: AI_Expl_Incl
fields.label: Explanation shown
fields.help: true if the AI's output came with an explanation: a rationale, highlighted evidence, feature importance, counterfactuals, a walk-through of the analysis

fields.name: AI_Expl_Type
fields.label: Explanation type
fields.help: modality of the explanation: Text (free-text rationale), Image (highlighted regions, saliency maps, screenshots), Numeric (feature weights, scores); empty when no explanation was shown

fields.name: AI_Conf_Incl
fields.label: Confidence shown
fields.help: true if the AI's confidence, probability or uncertainty was shown to the human

fields.name: Final_Decision
fields.label: Final decision
fields.help: who produces the answer that is scored: Human (the AI advises or is consulted and the human answers — includes free chat use) or AI (the AI's output is the final answer, e.g. the human's input feeds the AI, or a fixed rule fuses independent human and AI answers without either seeing the other)

fields.name: Division_Labor
fields.label: Division of labour
fields.help: true if items were split between human and AI: the AI handles some cases alone and the human others, cases are delegated, or only a verifier-selected subset goes to humans; false if the human judged every item with AI input

fields.name: Interaction_Mode
fields.label: Interaction mode
fields.help: (beyond the original codebook) how the human and the AI were combined in this condition

options.label: AI output shown before or while the human decides
Human decides first, then sees the AI output and may revise
Human uses the AI freely as a tool (chat, queries, drafting)
Independent human and AI answers combined by a rule; neither sees the other
Human verifies or edits AI-produced answers (the AI drafts first)

fields.name: measures
fields.label: Performance measures
fields.help: one row per performance measure reported for this condition. Each row carries the human-alone, AI-alone and human–AI values for THAT measure, on the same scale and exactly as printed. Leave a value null rather than guessing

columns.name: Perf_Metric
columns.label: Metric
columns.help: as named in the paper, with the unit when it is not obvious: 'Accuracy', 'Diagnostic reasoning score (%)', 'Sensitivity', 'AUC', 'Time per case (s)'

columns.name: Perf_Metric_Cleaned
columns.label: Metric class
columns.help: Accuracy (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, F1, AUC, agreement, Brier score), Quality (rated quality), Error (absolute or squared error), Error Rate (FPR, FNR, error %), Score (points or rubric scores that are not a proportion), Time

columns.name: Perf_Dir
columns.label: Direction
columns.help: Up if higher is better; Down if lower is better (errors, time)

columns.name: N_Human
columns.label: N human
columns.help: number of human PARTICIPANTS behind the human-alone value (people, never cases, items or ratings — put those in Notes)

columns.name: N_AI
columns.label: N AI
columns.help: (beyond the original codebook) number of independent AI RUNS behind the AI-alone value: 1 for a single deterministic run, 5 when each case was prompted five times — never the number of cases or items (put those in Notes)

columns.name: N_HumanAI
columns.label: N human–AI
columns.help: number of human PARTICIPANTS in this condition behind the human–AI value (people, never cases, items or ratings)

columns.name: Sd_Perf_AI
columns.label: SD AI
columns.help: 0 for a deterministic AI reported as a single value (as in the original codebook); the reported SD across runs for a generative model prompted repeatedly; otherwise null

columns.name: Est_ES
columns.label: Estimated
columns.help: true if any value in this row was read from a figure or computed rather than printed (SD = SE × √n, SD from a 95% CI, a mean of subgroup means); say how in Notes

columns.name: Notes
columns.label: Notes
columns.help: where the values come from and any derivation: 'Table 2; SD from SE 1.8 × √46'

groups.label: Design
groups.help: design, comparison type and sample size

groups.label: Task
groups.help: task description, task type, and the AI's input and output

groups.label: Participants
groups.help: who took part and how they were recruited

groups.label: AI system & presentation
groups.help: the AI system, model, what was shown to the human, who decided

groups.label: Results
groups.help: the measures table: right metric, right arm, same scale, correct N / mean / SD

derived.name: g_ai_vs_human
derived.label: AI alone vs human alone (Hedges' g)

complete.label: a human-alone, an AI-alone and a human+AI mean
